dedupe_keys.name: uwscatch urban water supply catchment contributions and hydrological statistics for large cities of the conterminous united states

description: Kristian Nelson and colleagues at PNNL and ORNL publish UWSCatCH for 116 cities with populations above 150,000 in the conterminous United States. It extends the Urban Water Blueprint with each surface-water catchment's contribution to urban supply, updated groundwater shares, NHDplusV2 intake reach codes, regulated and unregulated average flows, and nearby upstream USGS gauge identifiers. A 1/24-degree runoff grid represents mean reanalysis-simulated conditions for 1980–2012, masked to supplied watershed polygons. The February 2021 deposit offers complete and no-runoff ZIP variants free under CC BY 4.0. The inputs can connect urban demand to source catchments in water-supply simulations and were designed for the R package gamut. City coverage excludes smaller settlements, and long-term means do not describe drought-event dynamics. Detailed table schemas and uncertainty remain unknown from the landing page. No related catalogue record is explicitly identified; files were not downloaded.
